context: Focus+context time series navigator: a large main chart (50,000-point fractal random walk, LTTB-downsampled to 1,500 for rendering) paired with a compact minimap below; brush on minimap syncs with scroll-zoom on main chart; live stats bar shows visible-window summary; LOD system fades in dots and value labels at high zoom.
first_impression: Clean and unambiguous — two views with an immediately legible spatial relationship, a restrained two-color palette, and no competing visual elements.
what_works: The focus+context layout is textbook-clear: the brush selection rectangle in the minimap maps one-to-one to the main chart viewport, so the viewer never loses spatial orientation across 50,000 points. The stats bar (visible count, range, min, max, mean) delivers precise numerical context without cluttering the chart area, and the adaptive line weight (0.75px at high density, 1.5px at low) keeps the stroke readable across zoom levels.
what_doesnt: The minimap has no y-axis, so absolute value position in the full series is only inferrable from shape — intentional but silently loses amplitude context for the unzoomed view. Perceptual quality of the zoom/brush synchronization and the dot cross-fade LOD transition cannot be fully assessed from a static screenshot; jank or lag during fast scroll would be the main remaining risk.
